related_questions.question: Are COVID test kits free in BC?
related_questions.snippet: A number of community pharmacies in B.C. are distributing COVID-19 Rapid Test Kits free of charge to eligible British Columbians. These kits are rapid antigen tests that work by detecting the antigens (proteins) of the virus that causes COVID-19.

related_questions.question: How to get a COVID test in BC?
related_questions.snippet: Rapid Antigen Tests available at Community Pharmacies Rapid antigen tests are available for free at many community pharmacies. Anyone can ask for a kit. You don't have to show ID. If you can't go to a pharmacy, a friend or family member can pick up a test kit for you.

related_questions.question: How many days of COVID symptoms should I take a test?
related_questions.snippet: If you have symptoms, test immediately, and then test again per the instructions if your first result is negative. If you were exposed to someone who has COVID-19 and you do not have symptoms, wait at least 5 full days after your exposure before testing. If you test too early, you may have an inaccurate result.
